title: Spot a Repeated Value
statement:
Given an array of integers nums, return true if some value appears at least twice anywhere in the array, and false if every value is different.

The two copies do not have to be next to each other.

examples.why: 9 sits at index 1 and index 3. Checking only neighbours would miss it, because 2 is between them.
5 and -5 are different values. Every value appears once.

hints: Comparing every pair works but costs O(n²). What would let you answer "have I seen this value before?" instantly?
If the array were sorted, where would two equal values end up?
Walk the array once and keep a set of the values you have passed. The moment the current value is already in the set, you are done.

explain.intuition:
The question "is this value a repeat?" only needs to know which values came before. A hash set answers that in O(1), so one pass is enough: check, then add. It is the same trick as de-duplicating a list of IDs in the browser with new Set(ids); here you just stop early at the first collision.

Sorting also works: equal values land side by side, so one scan of neighbours finds them. It costs O(n log n) time but can run with no extra memory if you may reorder the input.
steps: For each value x in nums: if x is already in seen, return true.
Otherwise add x to seen and move on.
If the loop finishes, every value was new: return false.
pitfalls: Comparing only neighbours in the original order. That works only after sorting.
In JavaScript, calling nums.sort() with no comparator sorts as strings, and it also changes the caller's array. Copy first and pass (a, b) => a - b.

solutions.title: Compare every pair
solutions.idea: Check each pair (i, j) with i < j. Correct, but the number of pairs grows with n².

solutions.title: Sort, then look at neighbours
solutions.idea: After sorting, equal values are adjacent, so one scan finds a repeat.
solutions.space: O(n) for the copy (O(1) extra if sorting in place is allowed)

solutions.title: Hash set, one pass
solutions.idea: Remember every value seen so far; a value already in the set is the repeat.

followups: Return true only if the two copies are at most k indexes apart. How do you keep the set small?
The values arrive as a stream too large for memory. What could you trade for space, and what would you lose?
